Command: Be Perfect and Merciful as Your Father
Summary: Jesus' perfection command in its two Gospel forms: be perfect as your Father in heaven is perfect, and be merciful as your Father is merciful.
Commandment: Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect. Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful.
Application: Matthew's 'perfect' and Luke's 'merciful' are parallel forms of one command, merged here rather than split: the Father's indiscriminate kindness — sun and rain on just and unjust — is the standard, not mere rule-keeping.
Purpose: Scripture's own reason: the Father 'maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good' (Matthew 5:45).
Function: Matthew says perfect, Luke says merciful — one command in two forms, merged here rather than split. This comes from the New Testament, not from Sinai, so the old threefold division does not apply to it. Its goal was to make the Father's indiscriminate kindness the standard: sun and rain on just and unjust alike. The evil it addressed was love measured out only to the deserving, mercy rationed by merit. It restrained that evil by the Father's own pattern: be merciful as your Father is merciful.
